subtopics.title: Long-Term Causes: Bantu Education and Life Under Apartheid

questions.question: Which law, passed in 1953, set up a separate and unequal school system for black South Africans?
In the mid-1970s, government spending on a white pupil compared with a black pupil was:
options: More than ten times as much

questions.question: Soweto is a group of townships near:
Why is Afrikaans described as the "spark" rather than the only cause of the uprising?
options: Because pupils had no other complaints
Because the deeper causes were Bantu Education and apartheid as a whole
Because the uprising had nothing to do with schools
Because Afrikaans was never actually taught

subtopics.title: The Immediate Cause: The Afrikaans Medium Decree

questions.question: The Afrikaans Medium Decree of 1974 required that in black schools from Standard 5:
options: All subjects be taught in Afrikaans
Half the subjects be taught in Afrikaans and half in English

questions.question: Which Deputy Minister strongly supported the Afrikaans decree?
Which was a reason pupils objected to the decree?
options: Many teachers could not teach well in Afrikaans
Afrikaans was not spoken in South Africa

questions.question: Why did the decree feel like a political insult to many pupils?
options: Because Afrikaans was a foreign language from Europe
Because they associated Afrikaans with the government and the police
Because the decree was written in English
Because parents had asked for it

subtopics.title: Black Consciousness and the Student Leaders

questions.question: Black Consciousness was led by:
Black Consciousness taught that black people should:
options: Depend on white liberals to lead them
Take pride in their identity and lead their own struggle

questions.question: Who was the leading figure of the student action committee in 1976?
Why did the students keep the march plan secret from parents and teachers?
options: Because they planned to attack them
To protect them and to stop the police from hearing about it

options: They wanted to steal money for the march
They saw them as symbols of apartheid control that drained the community
They were told to by the police
They were owned by students' parents

questions.question: What is the main idea of this lesson?
options: The uprising was a riot with no causes
Students marched peacefully against Afrikaans and Bantu Education, and police shooting turned the protest into an uprising
